reviews.body:
Thanks for picking these up. The hint only adds text, and a failed mountinfo read falls back to the old message. I reviewed this by reading the code and did not run it.

Also:

- `read()` adds the hint only when `cuFileRead` raises. cuda-python's `check_status` raises only for a `-1` return. Other negative cuFile statuses reach the `received < 0` branch (`cufile_io.py:379`), which keeps the bare `status N` message. Adding the hint there would cover both.
- `fields[4].encode().decode("unicode_escape")` reads non-ASCII bytes as Latin-1, so `/mnt/données` becomes `/mnt/donnÃ©es`. A tmpfs mounted there gets no hint. The kernel escapes only space, tab, newline and backslash, as `\ooo`. `re.sub(r"\\([0-7]{3})", lambda m: chr(int(m[1], 8)), fields[4])` decodes just those.
- No test has two entries for the same mount point, where `>=` picks the later one, or an escaped mount point. One more `mountinfo` line for each in `test_filesystem_type_uses_longest_mount_prefix` would pin both.

review_comments.body:
When `TMPDIR` is unset, as it is by default on many systems, `"$TMPDIR"` expands to an empty string. The command then checks an empty path instead of `/tmp`, which is the case this section describes.

Suggest `findmnt -T "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" -o TARGET,FSTYPE`. For an input outside `TMPDIR`, `findmnt -T <input path>` checks that file directly.

On ramfs, and on tmpfs before Linux 6.6, the open fails earlier with `Invalid argument` rather than `HANDLE_NOT_REGISTERED`. Naming that error in the first paragraph would help those readers find this section.

From code reading: on ramfs, and on tmpfs before Linux 6.6, the file never reaches registration. Linux rejects an `O_DIRECT` open with `EINVAL` unless the file has `FMODE_CAN_ODIRECT` (`do_dentry_open` in `fs/open.c`). ramfs never sets it: `ram_aops` in `fs/libfs.c` has no `direct_IO`, and `ramfs_file_operations` has no `open`. tmpfs sets it in `shmem_file_open` since 6.6. Those opens fail at line 149, and the message at line 152 has no hint. So the `ramfs` entry in `_RAM_FILESYSTEMS` cannot produce a hint.

I expected the open failure to name the filesystem too. Suggest appending `_ram_filesystem_hint(selected)` to the message at line 152. A test modeled on `test_register_failure_on_tmpfs_names_filesystem`, with `os.open` raising `OSError(errno.EINVAL, ...)`, would cover it.
